44848.why:
A close spelling of a record's own name brings the record back, and the row says so.

Typing "Bridgport" (for Bridgeport) brings back ZZAUTOTEST Bridgeport Hauling, and the row carries the mark "≈ close match:" in front of the matched words, so the person can see at a glance that the spelling was only close and not exact. A second row came back the same way for a close match inside an address.

This is what the requirement asks for: when a match is close rather than exact, the matched words are still picked out and a subtle mark shows that it was close.

This was checked on staging because the Global Search test branch was merged into staging and then deleted. The search window, its tabs and its result rows all work there.

96844.why:
A close spelling of a CONTACT PERSON's name on a customer now works.

Typing "Oknokwo" (for Marlene Okonkwo, the contact on ZZAUTOTEST Bridgeport Hauling) and opening the Customers tab brings back exactly one row: ZZAUTOTEST Bridgeport Hauling, reading "Contact match: ≈ close match: Marlene Okonkwo". So the row comes back, it tells you it matched on a contact rather than the customer's own name, it shows you which contact, and it marks the spelling as only close - every part of what this check asks for.

This was checked on staging because the Global Search test branch was merged into staging and then deleted. The search window, its tabs and its result rows all work there.

55660.why:
Two of the three searches work, one does not.

Typing a piece from the middle of the company name ("idgepor" for Bridgeport) brings back ZZAUTOTEST Bridgeport Hauling, marked as a close match. Typing a piece from the middle of the address ("estrelw" for Kestrelway) brings it back too.

Typing a piece from the middle of the town name ("ernva" for Fernvale) brings back NOTHING AT ALL - the Customers tab reads zero. Two different customers live in Fernvale on this shop, and neither is found.

This is the difference the check was written to catch: the old search matched the letters you typed anywhere inside the record, so a piece from the middle of any word found it. The new one scores how similar the whole thing is, and a short piece from the middle of a short word scores too low to come back.

A report for this was already raised and the product team closed it OBSOLETE, so no new report is being written and nothing is waiting on your go-ahead for a ticket. What IS waiting on you is the check itself: if the behaviour is intended, this check is now wrong and should be retired or its wording changed. I cannot change what a check expects on my own.

55685.why:
Typing one person's name brings back a crowd of other names.

Typing "Marlene" and reading the Customers tab gives eleven customers. Only two of them have anything to do with Marlene: ZZAUTOTEST Marlene Freight Lines, and ZZAUTOTEST Bridgeport Hauling whose contact is Marlene. The other nine do not contain the word at all - among them Martens' Diesel Repair, contacts called Darlene and Charlene, and an address on Charlene Station.

Beyond the customers, the whole list also offers marine battery terminals, because they contain "MARINE". Somebody looking up a customer by name has to read past eight or nine records that have nothing to do with what they typed.

53601.why:
A part that the shop lists in its supplier catalogue but has never stocked cannot be found by searching.

The part is definitely there: the catalogue holds "ZZAUTOTEST Airline Coupler Vernway", part number ZZT-77-3300, and the catalogue's own list finds it by either the word or the number. This was checked directly before judging, so the result is not a missing-record problem.

Searching for "Vernway" in the search window brings back one row, and it is a different company (Vernal Diesel & Fleet Repair) offered as a close spelling. Searching the exact part number ZZT-77-3300 brings back nothing at all.

This is the change the check calls the highest-risk difference between the old search and the new one. The old search covered every part in the catalogue whether or not it had ever been on the shelf. The new one only looks at parts the shop stocks. A parts clerk searching for a part they have never bought before will be told it does not exist.

A report for this was already raised and the product team closed it OBSOLETE, so no new report is being written and nothing is waiting on your go-ahead for a ticket. What IS waiting on you is the check itself: if the behaviour is intended, this check is now wrong and should be retired or its wording changed. I cannot change what a check expects on my own.

53476.why:
Almost right, with one number still showing the true total.

What is right: every individual tab caps at twenty - Work orders (20), Customers (20), Assets (20), Parts (20), Vendors (20), Part sales (20), Purchase orders (20), Vendor invoices (20) - for a search matching far more than that. And the "Show all" link now carries no number at all, so it cannot overstate anything.

What is not: the All tab reads "All (160)". The check says no count anywhere in the window may read higher than twenty, and a hundred and sixty does. It is the eight capped counts added together, so it is not a true total either - it is a number that means nothing to the person reading it.

45160.why:
Nothing is recorded when somebody picks a search result.

A search was run, a result was clicked, and every request the page made was watched. The only thing that looks like a record is a Google Analytics message - and it carries the event name "page_view" and does not mention search anywhere. The same message fires when you simply walk to the Parts page without searching at all, so it is an ordinary page view, not a record of the search selection. Nothing is sent to ShopView's own system about the choice that was made.

So there is no way to learn what people search for, what they pick, or whether the search is helping them.

Worth knowing: the written requirements for this version say under Non-Goals that there will be no logging of what people see or click in this release, and the story that would have built it was closed OBSOLETE. So this is almost certainly intended, and this check - which was written against the OLD search - is the thing that is now out of date rather than the product. Retiring it or rewording it is your call; I cannot change what a check expects on my own.

55716.why:
Re-checked from scratch on staging, with records built for the purpose. The most recently touched record does not come first, and touching a record does not move it at all.

Five customers were set up whose names all begin with the same made-up word, so the search has nothing but recency to separate them. Ordered by when they were last touched, newest first, they are: Alpha Hauling (5:32:43pm), Beta Hauling (5:32:25pm), Hauling (5:30:04pm), then two older ones from this afternoon.

The search returns them in this order: Hauling, Beta Hauling, Alpha Hauling, Transport Two, Transport One. The most recently touched of them all, Alpha Hauling, comes third.

Alpha was then edited, which made it the newest by a clear margin, and the search was run again after several minutes to allow for any delay in the search catching up. The order did not change by a single place.

A report for this was already raised and the product team closed it OBSOLETE, and you said to leave it and not re-open it. So nothing is being raised. This result simply replaces the old one, which was measured on the test branch that has since been deleted, with a fresh measurement on staging.

The records used are all named beginning ZZTIEBREAK and have been left in place so this can be re-run without setting it up again.
